newsitem.title: INDIA: India's foreign currency reserves cross $20.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: India's foreign currency reserves cross $20.0 bln.

text.p: India's foreign currency reserves rose to $20.09 billion as on March 6, up from $19.69 billion on February 28, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Monday.

"During the current financial year so far, foreign currency assets increased by $3,042 million despite outflows to the extent of $1,234 million towards IDB (India Development Bonds) redemption," an RBI statement said.
Dealers said the rise in currency reserves reflected RBI's continued dollar purchases from the inter-bank forex market.
The RBI has been buying dollars since last year to arrest the rupee from gaining from an oversupply of dollars and a slowdown in dollar demand from Indian importers.
